title: Data-driven prediction of ultimate tensile strength in low alloy steel: A machine learning approach
abstract: In this research work, a data-driven approach was performed to predict the ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of low-alloy steel using machine learning. A large industrial dataset of over 44,000 samples was first cleaned to 41,924 samples by systematic data cleaning to ensure high-quality input for analysis. Statistical analysis via Pearson correlation and scatterplots revealed significant correlations between UTS and the key alloying elements, including carbon, manganese, and total alloy content. To find the best model, eight regression algorithms were compared using cross-validation, and the Random Forest Regressor revealed the best results with an R2 of 0.971 and MAE of 4.91 MPa on the test set. Confidence intervals based on model variance were introduced to assess prediction uncertainty. Additionally, a simplified model using only the three most influential features (Mn, Total, Nb) demonstrated comparable performance, highlighting the feasibility of reduced-feature models. Moreover, individual and collective variations of the critical elements were used for sensitivity analyses and additional information was provided on their effects on tensile strength. In this study, the potential of machine learning to revolutionize alloy design was demonstrated through the ability to make instant predictions and optimizations of mechanical properties and significantly reducing the reliance on massive experimental testing.
